name: effort-router
description: Saves time and money by running each task at the lowest reasoning effort that does it well. Your session's own model assesses each of your first prompts, knowing what each level can do on that model, and the session goes to the level that gets the work done fastest and cheapest. Then it locks. Subagents get their own level, chosen by the agent that starts them. The footer shows what it's doing, and /er report shows where your effort went.

promptsToAssess.title: Prompts to assess
promptsToAssess.description: How many of a session's first prompts the router assesses before it locks the level. Unlock in the band starts a fresh set.

highestLevel.title: Highest level
highestLevel.description: The highest effort the router picks. xhigh (default): max rarely does better than xhigh on the current models and can overthink. Choose max to allow it. If your own effort setting is higher, the router can pick up to it.

routeSubagents.title: Route subagents
routeSubagents.description: Give each subagent its own effort level: the agent starting it says what the subagent needs on the model it runs on. An agent whose definition sets an effort keeps it, and Haiku agents are left alone. Off: subagents use the session level.

rules.title: Routing rules
rules.description: Your own routing rules in plain words. Keep a line that is exactly $defaults to build on the built-in rules, or leave it out to replace them. A ~/.claude/effort-router.md file overrides this. In managed settings, this is how an organisation adds its rules for everyone.
